properties.name: Two constructor-shape refusals met while working, both instances of classes already on the record: add_artifact cannot set a checksum, and delete_edge refuses the endpoint types create_edge requires
properties.statement:
CAPTURED UNDER rule:a-reflow2-tool-failure-met-while-working-is-captured-as-a-to-do, 2026-09-07, while registering a field report and repairing a wrongly typed edge. Neither cost more than one round trip; both are recorded because the rule is that a refusal met here is a refusal a user's agent meets in their own design.

(1) add_artifact REFUSES `checksum`: "unknown field `checksum`, expected one of `id`, `name`, `artifact_type`, `location`". The Artifact schema declares `checksum`, link_artifact accepts one and its own skill says ALWAYS SUPPLY IT because it is the baseline that makes a later edit detectable, and set_artifact_checksum exists to change one later - but the plain constructor cannot set the first one. The workaround is create_node with a props bag, which is what was used. THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE DEFECT A USER REPORTED THE SAME DAY (fact:defect-a-declared-property-can-be-unreachable-and-invisible-to-the-reach-instrument-when-a-default-populates-it): a declared property that no typed constructor offers. It is invisible to the reachability instrument for the same reason those two were - most artifacts carry a checksum, so the property reads as heavily used, and the instrument only reports properties nothing has ever written.

(2) delete_edge REFUSES `from_type` and `to_type`: "unknown field `from_type`, expected one of `edge_type`, `from_id`, `to_id`". create_edge REQUIRES both. So the call that removes an edge and the call that makes one disagree about the shape of an edge, and the natural move - copy the create call, change the verb - fails. An instance of the surface-consistency class in dec:idea-one-way-to-name-which-node-across-the-tool-surface, which surveyed 44 write tools carrying two or more id/type parameters and ruled aliases onto the RELATION tools; delete_edge was not among them because it takes fewer fields, not more, and the convention as stated does not say what a tool should do with a field it does not need.

WHY THE SECOND ONE IS DEFENSIBLE AS BUILT: an edge is identified by its two ids and its type, so the endpoint types are genuinely redundant for a delete, and deny_unknown_fields is what catches a real typo. The friction is not that the field is absent, it is that nothing says so at the moment of the mistake - the refusal lists the legal fields and leaves the caller to infer that the two it dropped were unnecessary rather than misspelled. That is exactly wish #37 from the same day's field report (dec:idea-a-rejected-field-says-whether-it-moved-or-was-never-there), now met from inside the project as well as from outside it.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: no sweep was run for other constructors that cannot set a declared property of their own type, or for other pairs of tools that disagree about a field's necessity. Both are the same measurement the unfused reachability instrument would take, and it has not been taken.
